cleanIntro: The DEFCAN-9 and DEFCAN-45 are SEALED pistol-caliber suppressors. CMMG says so in one sentence for both cans, and its book prints no procedure that opens the body, so nothing in this guide does. What CMMG does publish is real maintenance on the outside of that sealed tube: the can off the host on its 3-lug quick-detach mount, the 3-lug mount unscrewed from the body so it, the body and the blast chamber can be cleaned and oiled, a bore brush with solvent but NEVER a patch, an optional solvent soak, and a flush routine for a can that has been in water. CMMG's interval is before and after every use. The two cans differ in caliber: the DEFCAN-9 is a 9mm can with a 1/2-28 3-lug adapter, the DEFCAN-45 a .45 ACP can with a 0.578-28 adapter, and CMMG says the two 3-lug mounts are not cross compatible. Fitting the 3-lug adapter to the barrel is a one-time job in CMMG's book, not part of cleaning, and is not in this guide.

steps.title: ⛔ Host unloaded and the ACTION OPEN before the can comes off
steps.action: Make the host firearm safe first: unloaded, with the action OPEN so you can see it is clear. CMMG asks for the action open specifically, every time the DEFCAN goes on or comes off.
steps.prose: Everything in this guide happens with a hand at the muzzle end. That is why the action stays open.
steps.quote: NOTE: Make sure firearm is unloaded and the action is open to verify clear before removing your DEFCAN from the host firearm.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-9 / DEFCAN-45 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Removal, printed p.5

steps.title: ⛔ Let it COOL, or wear gloves
steps.action: Let the suppressor cool to the temperature of the room before you take it off or work on it. If it has to come off hot, wear protective gloves. Gloves also help at the mount, where the can and the muzzle device can pinch a finger as they come apart.
steps.prose: A can after a string of fire is hot enough to burn badly, and it does not look hot.
steps.caution: The point of attachment or detachment can present the potential for pinching and caution should be taken, including wearing protective gloves, to avoid severe injury at the pinch point.
steps.quote: Allow suppressor to cool to ambient temperature before removal and/or service. If suppressor must be removed or installed while hot, protective gloves should be worn.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-9 / DEFCAN-45 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Safety notices, printed p.4

steps.title: Know the rating: full-auto rated, no minimum barrel length
steps.action: Both DEFCANs are full-auto rated, and CMMG sets no minimum barrel length for either. What does matter is caliber: the DEFCAN-9 goes on a 9mm host with its 9mm 3-lug adapter, the DEFCAN-45 on a .45 ACP host with its .45 adapter, and the two mounts do not interchange.
steps.prose: The book's spelling of minimum is quoted as printed.
steps.quote: The DEFCAN-9 and DEFCAN-45 are full auto rated with no mimimum barrel length restrictions.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-9 / DEFCAN-45 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Full auto firing schedule, printed p.5

steps.title: Off the host: press the locking release tab, can off
steps.action: Press the locking release tab on the suppressor mount, then take the DEFCAN off. The 3-lug muzzle adapter stays on the barrel.
steps.prose: Mind the pinch point at the mount as the can comes away.
steps.quote: Press the locking release tab on the suppressor mount.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-9 / DEFCAN-45 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Removal, printed p.5

steps.title: 3-lug mount off the body: counter-clockwise
steps.action: Hold the DEFCAN body firmly in one hand and turn the 3-lug mount counter-clockwise to loosen it, then unscrew it from the body. CMMG's regular maintenance includes cleaning the mount, the suppressor body and the blast chamber, and those surfaces are only reachable with the mount off.
steps.prose: The mount went on at 30 ft-lb, so expect it to be tight. The book names no tool for this; it does not ask you to put the can in a vise.
steps.aside: Firmly grasp the DEFCAN body in one hand.
steps.quote: Turn the 3-lug mount counter-clockwise to loosen.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-9 / DEFCAN-45 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — HUB Mount Removal, printed p.6

steps.title: ⛔ That is as far as it goes: the body is SEALED
steps.action: Nothing else comes apart. CMMG states that both DEFCANs are a sealed suppressor design, and its book prints no procedure for opening the body. With the can off the host and the mount off the body, everything below is cleaning on a closed tube.
steps.prose: A sealed can is not a can you have failed to open. If something inside is wrong, it goes back to CMMG.
steps.quote: Both DEFCAN-9 and DEFCAN-45 are a sealed suppressor design, eliminating much of the disassembly required for general cleaning and maintenance.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-9 / DEFCAN-45 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.5

steps.title: Inspect it: bore, a shake, the outside
steps.action: Look through the bore for any obstruction or foreign object. Shake the can and listen for anything broken or loose inside. On a sealed can that is the only internal check you have. Then check the outside for dents or other damage. CMMG wants this before and after every use.
steps.prose: A rattle, a blocked bore or a dented tube means the can does not go back on the host until CMMG has seen it.
steps.aside: Inspect the exterior for any signs of external damage such as dents.
steps.quote: Shake the suppressor and listen to check for any broken or detached internal parts.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-9 / DEFCAN-45 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.6

steps.title: Mount, body and blast chamber: clean and lightly oil
steps.action: With the mount off, clean the QD mount's surfaces, the suppressor body and the blast chamber, then put a light coat of oil on them. The mount threads get anti-seize.
steps.prose: Light oil means light. Carbon on these surfaces is what turns a solid lockup into play.
steps.quote: Remove, clean, and lightly oil the QD mount surfaces, suppressor body, and blast chamber.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-9 / DEFCAN-45 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.6

steps.title: Bore: brush and solvent, NEVER a patch
steps.action: Use a bore brush and gun cleaning solvent to take carbon buildup and fouling out of the suppressor bore. Do not run a cleaning patch through it: a patch can lodge inside the sealed can and cause damage the next time the host is fired. Do not put the can in an ultrasonic cleaner either; CMMG says it can damage the finish.
steps.prose: The brush comes back out on the rod. A patch has nothing holding it.
steps.caution: NOTE: Suppressor should NOT be cleaned in an ultrasonic cleaner. Damage to finish may occur.
steps.quote: A bore brush and gun cleaning solvent may be used to remove any carbon buildup or fouling from the bore of the suppressor.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-9 / DEFCAN-45 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.6
steps.warn: NOTE: Do NOT run cleaning patches through the bore of the suppressor as they could become lodged inside the suppressor and cause damage upon firing.

steps.title: Stubborn buildup: soak, then stand it HUB-threads DOWN to drain
steps.action: For buildup the brush will not shift, CMMG allows a solvent soak with the QD mount off the body. Afterwards stand the can on a clean towel with the HUB threaded end down and the front cap up, so standing solvent runs down the baffle stack and out through the bore hole. Let it dry completely before anything is oiled or put back together.
steps.prose: Solvent left inside a sealed can has nowhere to go but out the muzzle the next time you fire it. Give it the time to drain and dry.
steps.aside: Allow the suppressor to completely dry before lightly oiling surfaces, applying anti-seize to threads, and re-assembling.
steps.quote: If soaking the suppressor in solvent to remove stubborn buildup, remove the QD mount from the body and stand the suppressor up on a clean towel with the HUB threaded side facing down and front cap facing up to allow any standing solvent to run down the baffle stack and drain through the bore hole.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-9 / DEFCAN-45 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.6

steps.title: If it has been in water: drain, flush hot, dry, oil
steps.action: Do this as soon as you can after the can has been used in or exposed to water. Let it drain completely. Soak and flush it with very hot water and detergent, draining between rounds, three to four times at least. Then soak and flush it with clean boiling water. Dry it with compressed air through the can if you have it, or overnight in an oven on a warm setting if time allows. Once it is thoroughly dry, lubricate the mount and suppressor surfaces and put anti-seize on the threads.
steps.prose: Do not shoot it wet unless you truly have to. CMMG's word is absolutely necessary.
steps.aside: After the suppressor has been thoroughly dried, lubricate the mount and suppressor surfaces, apply anti-seize to the threads, and re-assemble.
steps.quote: Soak and flush the suppressor with very hot water and a detergent. Drain and repeat this procedure a minimum of 3-4 times.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-9 / DEFCAN-45 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Maintenance after water exposure, printed p.7
steps.warn: Allow to drain completely and DO NOT use the suppressor unless absolutely necessary.

deepAbsentReason: CMMG's book calls both the DEFCAN-9 and the DEFCAN-45 a sealed suppressor design (printed p.5) and prints no procedure that opens the body. The deepest work it publishes is taking the 3-lug HUB mount off the body (printed p.6), a solvent soak (printed p.6), and the flush after water exposure (printed p.7). CMMG makes those part of its regular maintenance, and they are in the routine lane above. A can that rattles, is blocked or is damaged goes back to CMMG: the book asks the owner to contact CMMG Customer Service to arrange a return, and not to return it to the retailer (printed p.8). This listing therefore has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: INSPECTION — BEFORE AND AFTER USE
tasks: Look through the bore for obstructions or foreign objects.
Shake the can and listen for anything broken or detached inside.
Check the outside for dents or other damage.

cleaning.name: MOUNT, BODY & BLAST CHAMBER
tasks: Clean the mount's surfaces, the suppressor body and the blast chamber.
A light coat of oil on those surfaces; anti-seize on the mount threads.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Bore brush and gun cleaning solvent for carbon and fouling.
⛔ Never run a cleaning patch through the bore.
Do not clean the can in an ultrasonic cleaner.

cleaning.name: SOLVENT SOAK & DRY
tasks: Only for stubborn buildup, with the QD mount off the body.
Stand it on a clean towel, HUB threads down, front cap up, to drain.
Completely dry before oiling, anti-seize or reassembly.

cleaning.name: AFTER WATER EXPOSURE
tasks: As soon as possible: drain completely.
Very hot water and detergent, soak and flush, at least 3–4 times.
A soak and flush with clean boiling water.
Dry with compressed air, or overnight in an oven on warm.
Once thoroughly dry: lubricate the mount and surfaces, anti-seize on the threads.

reassembly: Mounting surfaces and threads clean; a light coat of oil on the mount surfaces and a thin coat of anti-seize on the threads, to prevent galling or seizing.
Thread the 3-lug mount into the DEFCAN body clockwise, taking care not to cross-thread it.
Host firearm unloaded, with the action open to verify clear.
Slide the rear of the suppressor over the installed 3-lug muzzle device until it is firmly seated; it can go on in any orientation.
Listen for the click: the locking release tab pops up when the DEFCAN is fully seated and locked.
fncheck: With the host firearm unloaded and the action open: the DEFCAN went on with a click and the locking release tab has popped up, which is CMMG's sign that the can is fully seated and locked. Look through the bore for obstructions, shake the can and listen for anything loose inside, and check the mount was tightened to 30 ft-lb if it was off the body.
